scope: The four changed public-route gameplay screens in desktop, narrow desktop, phone landscape, and phone portrait, reviewed at original resolution after machine gates passed. Unchanged selection screens remain part of the ordered hash so any unrelated pixel change invalidates this record.
resolvedFindings: The organic floor substantially removes the prior checkerboard and hard cell seams.
The portrait objective compass no longer overlaps the forge or Hexer.
The quieter floor slightly improves actor-to-terrain contrast, and no major actor-to-actor clipping remains in the four static frames.
rejectedFindings: The opening remains an unbounded empty field containing one forge and scattered props rather than a coherent room, corridor, entrance, or layered encounter space.
Forge, actors, enemies, props, and controls still disagree in perspective, rendering sharpness, lighting, outline treatment, and apparent scale.
The actor arrangement reads as a static vertical display without a clear threat direction, environmental story, lighting focus, or memorable opening beat.
Ashfang reads as a dead or prone flaming carcass; Stonekin is overly dominant and Hexer partly merges into the forge.
Mobile labels and ornate controls remain difficult to read at phone size, and the compass still lacks a clear visual relationship to its target.
promotionRule: This rejection applies only while both the contract and ordered screenshot-set hashes match. Any pixel or contract change invalidates it and returns the gallery to candidate; no machine metric can override a matching rejection.
